doc.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: Preferring first albums and one-of-a-kind artists
summary: Dorn says he likes first albums and original artists with world-class chops.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Well you said you’ve always been drawn to a world class artist that has — you like to see them when they’re stretching, early on?

Well I like first albums. I like world class artists who are original. So I’ve always been drawn to anything from Rufus Harley to Bette Midler to Leon Redbone to Rahsaan. That’s what I like — one of a kind artists with world class chops. And I like them in the
early stages, because you never get the innocence again and you never get the reach again. Once they’re successful they’re not at that place anymore. So the first albums are what I dig the most.
